newsitem.title: EGYPT: Arafat discusses Mideast peace crisis with Mubarak.
newsitem.headline: Arafat discusses Mideast peace crisis with Mubarak.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Thursday discussed the Middle East peace process, which has been in deep freeze since Israel began building a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa told reporters the two leaders also reviewed clashes between Palestinians and Israeli troops in the West Bank and Gaza.
A senior aide to Arafat said on Wednesday that Egyptian efforts to revive Israeli-PLO peace talks were near collapse and complained that Washington had withdrawn from peacemaking.

Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, secretary-general of the Palestinian Authority, blamed Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for the failure of an Egyptian mediation drive and warned that the West Bank and Gaza were on the verge of an explosion.
Israeli troops on Wednesday wounded 37 youths protesting against posters pasted on Palestinian shops on Saturday. Moslems say the posters insult Islam's Prophet Mohammad and the Koran.
"The situation in the occupied territories and the situation in the peace process are not in a good shape," Moussa said.

"The contacts between the Palestinians and the Israelis will continue to probe some of the issues that are on the table, the confidence building measures, the question of settlements and so on. We are waiting for the results of those contacts.
"I can't add anything more than this about whether there will be progress or a breakthrough," he added.
Peace talks between Israel and the Palestinians collapsed in March after the Jewish state began building a new settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.
Egypt has stepped in as the main mediator between the two sides over the past few weeks as a result of what many Arabs perceive as a lack of U.S. interest in the peace process.

Mubarak has sent his senior political adviser, Osama el-Baz, to see Palestinian and Israeli leaders several times in an attempt to bring them back to the negotiating table but both sides say there is still a gap between their positions.
Mubarak said Egypt would not for the time being resume its negotiating efforts but that contacts between the two sides would bring about progress soon.
